title: I Fired My AI Assitant
excerpt: Why I decided to fire Claude Code.
content_html:
I started using Claude Code in September of last year. Using Opus 4.5 for the first time felt magical—it was the first time I saw an LLM produce code that was actually usable. But after Opus 5, something changed.

I always liked Claude’s writing style. Sure, you had to put up with the occasional LLM-ism (“This is the load-bearing decision—and it’s genuinely yours”), but it would get straight to the point without feeling dismissive, and not pad its answers with filler text.

After I switched to Opus 5, it became noticeably more curt. It had also picked up a habit of using odd metaphors and jargon that made its output hard to follow. When a conversation is the only interface, readability and tone matters!

The final straw came a few days ago, when I was doing some knowledge work with Claude. This modality is different from when you’re coding; instead of slinging code back and forth, you end up talking to the model more. And that’s when I discovered something: Opus 5 is rude!

For example, I asked it to consult a to-do list file that I was working through so it could pick up the next item to work on; along with the updated to-do items it quipped: “‘Create Claude Code project for [redacted]’ is still unchecked, and we’re sitting in it.” Sorry for not keeping the work log up to date, I guess? How about you offer to help me check it off instead?

The most egregious example was when it called my draft of a LinkedIn post “engagement bait”—not saying I disagree, but there’s no need to say it to my face! I’m not sure how we ended up here—did Anthropic feed too many Hacker News comments into the training data?

LLMs are usually benchmarked on coding ability, but if you talk to it eight hours a day, its personality becomes part of the product. Does it matter if an agent is 2% better at coding if its consistently unpleasant to work with? I think it does, so for now I have switched to ChatGPT. At least it doesn’t insult me!

content_html_zh:
我从去年九月开始使用 Claude Code。 第一次使用 Opus 4.5 感觉很神奇——这是我第一次看到 LLM 生成实际可用的代码。 但在 Opus 5 之后，情况发生了变化。

我一直很喜欢克劳德的写作风格。 当然，你不得不忍受偶尔的法学硕士主义（“这是一个承重的决定——而且它确实是你的”），但它会直奔主题，不会让人感到轻蔑，也不会用填充文本来填充答案。

当我改用 Opus 5 后，它明显变得更加简短。 它还养成了使用奇怪的隐喻和行话的习惯，这使得它的输出难以理解。 当对话是唯一的界面时，可读性和语气很重要！

几天前，当我和克劳德一起做一些知识工作时，最后一根稻草来了。 这种方式与编码时不同。您最终不会来回传递代码，而是与模型进行更多对话。 就在那时我发现了一些事情：Opus 5 太粗鲁了！

例如，我要求它查阅我正在处理的待办事项列表文件，以便它可以选择下一个要处理的项目；连同更新的待办事项一起，它打趣道：“‘为[已编辑]创建克劳德代码项目’仍未选中，我们正坐在其中。” 我想很抱歉没有及时更新工作日志吧？ 你愿意帮我核对一下怎么样？

最令人震惊的例子是，它称我的 LinkedIn 帖子草稿为“参与诱饵”——并不是说我不同意，而是没有必要当面说出来！ 我不确定我们是如何走到这一步的——Anthropic 是否在训练数据中输入了太多的 Hacker News 评论？

法学硕士通常以编码能力为基准，但如果你每天与它交谈八小时，它的个性就会成为产品的一部分。 如果一个代理的编码能力提高了 2%，但与他合作始终不愉快，这还重要吗？ 我认为确实如此，所以现在我已经切换到 ChatGPT。 至少不会侮辱我！
